subject: RFP: commercial clarification - committed volumes, surge protection, and true-up cadence
messages:

Subject: RFP Qs - commercial section (volume bands, surge protection, true-up)

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the quick turn on the RFP submission. A few follow-ups from procurement and finance on Section 3 (pricing):

1) We want to understand nozzle pricing across burst events. If our monthly peak (99th percentile) can be 3-4x baseline in certain months, how do you protect our bill volatility? Do you offer a "surge protection" buffer or pre-burn pool?

2) True-up cadence: our finance team prefers quarterly true-ups and an annual reconciliation. Is quarterly allowed vs. monthly?

3) Discounts and escalator: clarify how incremental discounts apply if we step up committed volumes mid-year. Are mid-year committal increases pro-rated?

4) Token price examples: please provide an illustrative table (baseline, committed tier price, overage rate, burst buffer rate) for a 5M token/month baseline with 2x and 4x surge profiles.

I've attached the relevant RFP excerpt (Novus_RFP_Section3.pdf). Can you get us a concrete worked example and the preferred contract language you'd ask to see for surge protection?

Best,
Daniel
Procurement, Novus Financial

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the clear list. We reviewed with finance and legal and put together a compact response + a worked example (attached: Redwood_Usage_Pricing_2026.xlsx). Summary below; happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk the numbers next week.

High-level options we typically propose (choose one or mix):

- Annual Commit + Surge Protection Pool (recommended for predictable cost): Customer commits to an annual token volume; we amortize monthly. A separate surge-protection pool equal to 15% of the annual commit is reserved to absorb transient spikes at a reduced overage rate for up to X months per year. Pool renews annually.

- Monthly Commit with Quarterly True-up (flexible): Customer sets a baseline monthly commit. True-ups are quarterly (finance-friendly). Overage billed monthly but credited retroactively at quarter-end based on aggregate quarter usage vs. committed volume.

- Pre-purchased Burst Credits (on-demand): Customer purchases discrete burst credit bundles (e.g., 500k-token bundles) at a discounted rate to be consumed when needed; unused credits roll-forward for up to 6 months.

Worked example (from spreadsheet): baseline 5,000,000 tokens/month (60M annual)
- Committed annual price (anchor): $0.0008 / token (applies to committed volume)
- Surge Protection Buffer: 15% of annual commit (9M tokens) available for up to 3 high-months; overage rate when consuming buffer: $0.00095 / token (10% uplift to committed)
- Standard overage rate (outside buffer): $0.0012 / token (50% uplift vs committed)
- Burst credit bundle price: $0.0009 / token (500k increments, roll-forward 6 months)

Mid-year increases: pro-rata pricing on incremental committed volume for the remainder of contract period; tiered discount ladder still applies (we can ladder to preserve incentives).

True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups are supported under our standard commercial terms; final reconciliation annually. If you need monthly true-ups for operational reasons we can support that too but it changes invoicing cadence.

Contract language we propose for surge protection (plain-English summary):
"A Surge Protection Pool equal to 15% of Customer's committed annual tokens will be available to cover temporary spikes. Usage charged against the Pool will incur a reduced overage rate for up to three (3) billing months per 12-month period. Any Pool usage beyond those months will be invoiced at the standard overage rate."

Attachments: detailed table with month-by-month examples, amortization, and invoice mockups.

Let me know preferred time for a walk-through.

Thanks,

Ava — adding a short note on an optional structure that some of our mid-market customers have found useful; copied Daniel for visibility.

--- Forwarded message follows ---

Why this helps: it reduces headline overage exposure while preserving headroom for sudden growth.

Optional: Annuitized Credits + Rolling Carry-Forward
- Annuitized credits: customer purchases 12 monthly "credit units" equal to committed volume; each month unused credits roll into a short-term carry-forward bucket (max 2 months).
- Rolling Carry-Forward: up to 20% of a month's unused credits can be carried forward and used within the next two months before expiration. This reduces the need for high temporary overage charges in high-variance workloads.
- Pricing: annuitized committed token price = $0.00082/token; carry-forward consumption billed at committed price; once carry-forward exhausted, standard overage applies.

If Novus wants to cap exposure, we can also add a monthly spend ceiling that triggers temporary throttling (technical option) or an SLA-based credit if throttling occurs. Both are contract terms we can include in the SOW.

Karthik
Director, Commercials

Ava/Karthik —

Appreciate the detailed response and the worked example. Procurement likes the Annual Commit + Surge Protection Pool (the pool model gives us predictable finance impact). A couple of follow-ups before we include in the draft SOW:

1) Can you confirm the Pool usage reporting cadence (we want daily visibility with month-to-date consumption and a forecasted exhaustion date if current burn continues).
2) For the 15% pool you propose: can we have the contract call it a "surge buffer" with explicit language that usage beyond the 3-month allowance will be invoiced at the standard overage and will not be auto-deducted from the next year's commit? (finance compliance).
3) Pilot ask: can you provide a 3-month pilot at 50% of the committed price (applies to the pilot volume only) so we can validate peak patterns with our internal traffic generator?

If you can confirm those three points in writing we'll route a redline to legal and move to a term sheet.

Thanks,
Daniel
Procurement, Novus Financial
